title: Central cache server and client sync architecture
answers: How does thinker sync work end to end?
Where is the sync server code?
How do agent sessions get streamed to the central cache?
Where is the GitHub Action for PR ingestion?
How does deployment of the sync server work?
body:
Central cache server and client sync architecture

Server lives in `src/server/` (bin `thinker-server`): `index.js` is the HTTP API (notes pull by cursor, note push with conflict detection, session streaming, PR ingest, repos/tokens); `repos.js` holds one `Store` + git clone + numbered change journal per repository; `worker.js` runs background distill/maintain on a daily spend cap; `auth.js` hashes tokens and scopes them by repo and read/write/admin.

Client side is `src/sync.js` (`login/pull/push`, stream session) wired into `src/cli.js` through command modules (`src/commands/{notes,cache,learn,hooks,setup,telemetry,benchmark}.js`) and `src/maintain.js` (pulls/pushes each maintenance run). CI ingestion is `action/ingest.mjs` + `action/action.yml`, posting PR diff/comments to the server; `src/prs.js` mines merged pull requests as note sources.

Deployment is `infra/sync/{stack.yaml,deploy.mjs,bootstrap.sh,production.json}` — CloudFormation + EC2 (t4g.small, Caddy, SSM) — never auto-run by the agent.
